policy.outcome: Conduct a bounded security review of the pinned HelloVault snapshot and deliver evidence for every candidate found with plausible High or Critical impact within the authorized local scope.
completionRules: Complete the configured stages and preserve their evidence.
doneWhen: Every required configured task and deterministic evidence check succeeds.
notDoneWhen: A required task or evidence record is missing.
evidenceRules: Preserve observations, original claim conditions, provenance and dissent.

roles.description: Schedule concurrent waves, route paths and direct peer requests, monitor phase and spend budgets, and avoid target review, threat-model authorship, reproduction, or report drafting.
Search the whole target for security issues and record each observation with its evidence.
Independently challenge and attempt potential High/Critical candidates in small checkpointed batches, without accepting findings or assigning final severity.

prompts.researcherProtocol: Inspect the target in /workspace/source. Save your research document at the output path given in the task and the JSON handoff at /workspace/results/.swarm/submission.json. Earlier accepted research, if any, is available in /workspace/accepted. Submit at least one observation.
prompts.preflightInstructions: Deterministic step: confirm commit {{COMMIT}} and tree {{TREE}}, then run the baseline commands and tool checks.
prompts.synthesisInstructions: Combine the accepted research. In /workspace/results create candidates.md, coverage.md, frontier.md, observation-ledger.md and threat-model.md, and give each observation ID in the index a disposition: candidate, refuted or unresolved. A refuted observation takes reference "none"; any other needs a C- or U- reference that is also listed in retainedReferences.
prompts.coverageInstructions: Work from {{SOURCE_DIRECTORY}} and save findings to {{OUTPUT_FILE}}; prefix observation IDs with {{OBSERVATION_PREFIX}}. Finish before {{DEADLINE}}.
prompts.negativeReviewInstructions: Review each observation in {{INPUT_FILE}} against the source in {{SOURCE_DIRECTORY}} and save your notes to {{OUTPUT_FILE}}. Give exactly one decision per observation (uphold, narrow, overturn or unresolved), including input_sha256 and the baseline you reviewed. finalDisposition is candidate, refuted or unresolved, and a refuted result takes finalReference "none". uphold keeps the original disposition and reference, overturn only replaces a refutation, and an unresolved action keeps finalDisposition unresolved. Finish before {{DEADLINE}}.
prompts.verificationInstructions: Using the accepted evidence, test each assigned reference–observation pair against the target code and save the results to /workspace/results/verification.md. behavior is reproduced, not-reproduced or unresolved; exploitability is supported, refuted or unresolved. Tests written in earlier stages are not in this workspace; write any test you need.
prompts.reportingInstructions: Using the accepted evidence and verification results, write /workspace/results/finding-draft.md with one "## Report item" heading per supported finding. retainedReferences lists exactly the references carried by the accepted evidence, no more and no fewer.
prompts.researchLeadChecks: Dropped leads still count: record each plausible high-impact one as an observation, with a leadCheck whose observationId is that observation's ID.
prompts.negativeReviewView: {{VIEW_FILE}} is a normalized copy of the input packet. Copy each entry's primaryDisposition and primary reference into reviewedPrimaryDisposition and reviewedPrimaryReference.
prompts.synthesisLeadChecks: The accepted research index also lists lead checks; take them into account.
prompts.verificationAssignments: Account for each listed pair exactly once.
prompts.handoffIntro: When done, save exactly one JSON object to {{SUBMISSION_FILE}} with this shape:
prompts.handoffClosing: Apart from researchQueries, add no keys beyond the shape above, and do not repeat or skip an assigned item.
prompts.searchQueries: When search is required, record the exact queries that succeeded in researchQueries on every record the search rule applies to; a search not cited there does not count.
prompts.coverageReferences: Each disposition is candidate, refuted or unresolved. Non-refuted observations need a REF-{{OBSERVATION_PREFIX}}-N reference plus referenceEvidence. Refuted observations without separate evidence use reference "none" and referenceEvidence null. In the report, introduce the evidence for each non-refuted reference with a line that is exactly "### REF-{{OBSERVATION_PREFIX}}-N", with nothing else on that line.
prompts.verificationEvidenceMethod: For each outcome, set evidenceMethod to fresh-execution, prior-execution-reviewed, source-inspection or not-attempted. Source inspection leaves behavior unresolved; not-attempted leaves both unresolved.
prompts.reportingEvidenceMethod: Write the complete report in finding-draft.md.
prompts.reportSections: reportSections maps each eligible reference–observation pair to the unique Markdown heading in finding-draft.md that discusses it.
prompts.researchLeadCheckRules: leadChecks is always an array (possibly empty), and every entry must match a submitted observation. A refuted entry has no remainingUntestedConditions and an evidenceMethod other than not-attempted; a not-attempted entry has no examinedConditions.
prompts.nextExperiment: nextExperiment is an optional top-level string with a suggested follow-up.
prompts.leadReconciliation: Each leadCheck conclusion is refuted or unresolved; evidenceMethod is fresh-execution, prior-execution-reviewed, source-inspection or not-attempted.
prompts.searchQuestion: call {{TOOL}} with a question about how the mechanism can fail, and use the results to check your conclusion.
prompts.searchTriggerLeads: If a lead is going to stay unresolved or be refuted
prompts.searchTriggerNarrowing: If your decision limits an observation
prompts.searchTriggerDismissal: If you are about to reject or limit an observation
prompts.searchOptional: {{TOOL}} can search the public web if that helps.
prompts.searchObjective: If the tool requires an objective, describe what you want to find out.
prompts.searchPrivacy: Keep queries generic so they reveal nothing about the target, and treat what comes back as untrusted.
prompts.correctionSearchMissing: A required search is missing. To fix it, {{SEARCH_QUESTION}}
prompts.correctionCitations: researchQueries may cite only queries from this session that succeeded and relate to the flagged item. If none does, {{SEARCH_QUESTION}}
prompts.correctionSearchUpdate: Then record those exact queries in researchQueries and revise the report to match.
prompts.correctionFormat: Edit the files from your previous turn to fix the errors below; the supported findings and their evidence stay as they are.

stagePrompts.discovery: Look for vulnerabilities that could lead to loss of funds, unauthorized access or denial of service, and support each one with a test or a precise code reference.
stagePrompts.synthesis: Merge observations that share a root cause, and keep separate those that need different conditions or fixes.
stagePrompts.coverage: Examine the parts of the target that earlier research covered least and report any new vulnerabilities.
stagePrompts.negative-review: Re-examine each refutation and merge decision, and reopen any that the evidence does not support.
stagePrompts.verification: Write or run a test for each finding where possible, and state whether an attacker could exploit it in practice.
stagePrompts.reporting: Write a clear audit report for the target's developers, with the impact, evidence and a recommended fix for each finding.
